description: Everything the console observes, plus the launcher that starts it. The observation hooks POST each event to the console on its default port through a curl one-liner that always exits 0, so a console that isn't running costs nothing but a discarded connection refusal instead of a hook-error notice on every tool call. A POST that finds nothing listening hands off to console-restart.sh, which brings a crashed console back on what it last watched and stays silent either way. The launcher exits immediately unless a real team exists, except on the Workflow tool — a workflow forms no team, so that matcher points the console at the session that ran it instead. SessionStart also runs console-hint.sh, which replaces a console running an older build than the session loaded and, after a resume, tells a lead its teammates are gone; otherwise it says nothing. PreToolUse on TaskCreate and TaskUpdate also runs task-gate.sh, which gates a team8 task's metadata and a teammate's completion on the call's own input instead of observing anything. Timeouts are in seconds. The console's answer to a teammate's PostToolUse can carry added context: a reminder to report progress on a task that has sat unchanged for two minutes. A second PostToolUse hook, inbox-deliver.js, hands a teammate its unread messages as added context after each of its tool calls and marks them read, so the delivery at the end of its turn skips them. Hooks are user-scope, so its sh pre-filter starts node for teammates only: a teammate's agent_id is name@team, or a<name>-<16 hex> on 2.1.296, while a plain subagent's or workflow agent's is a<hex> with neither @ nor -, and the lead's hooks carry none. The filter reads agent_id only from the fields Claude Code writes ahead of tool_input, since stripping a prefix from a whole payload is quadratic in sh and a large tool response would hold the turn for seconds. The hooks module's wave notifier, wave-notify.ts, watches teammates' TaskUpdate calls: a second after a teammate completes a task it reads TaskList and the roster, and when a pending task is now unblocked and its owner is idle or not running, it submits one prompt that wakes the lead to dispatch it. It never changes a call. The module's entry, team8.tsx, registers that notifier and draws a band above the prompt: each teammate with a digit hotkey, its state and task, the task count and the console link; a digit opens the console on that teammate. It reads the roster, TaskList and the console's /health, never the files the console ingests.

hooks.command: curl -sS -m 5 -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- http://127.0.0.1:4823/hook 2>/dev/null || OCTO_PORT=4823 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/console-restart.sh"; exit 0
curl -sS -m 5 -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- http://127.0.0.1:4823/hook 2>/dev/null || OCTO_PORT=4823 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/console-restart.sh"; exit 0

input=$(cat); id=${input%%'"tool_input":'*}; id=${id#*'"agent_id":"'}; id=${id%%'"'*}; case "$id" in *@*|*-*) printf '%s' "$input" | node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/dist/hooks/inbox-deliver.js" 2>/dev/null;; esac; exit 0
